bug_semantics: When the Management API is enabled with its token omitted or empty, its middleware treats every request as authenticated and its HTTP server listens on all interfaces. A remote caller can POST an arbitrary exec string to /api/v1/cron; that string is persisted as CronJob.Exec and executed by the cron scheduler through shellExecCommand with the shell command flag (-c on Unix). Scheduled execution is sufficient for RCE, and later commit c580b68716a7cdc6a0e6702e5782c17d074a7978 also added POST /api/v1/cron/{id}/exec for immediate execution. No shell metacharacter neutralization or command allowlist intervenes.
flaw_origin: Single-parent feature commit c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 first added the externally reachable Management API and, in the same commit, added the empty-token allow-all branch plus the cron POST endpoint that copies untrusted req.Exec into a shell cron job. Its direct parent already had cron shell execution but had no core/management.go and therefore no Management API attack path. This is the smallest commit that completed the advisory's remote unauthenticated command-execution chain; it is not a move, refactor, revert, release/backport, merge, or decomposed squash.
ai_marker: BIC commit object c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 has author and committer chenhg5 <chenhonggui@wps.cn> and contains the exact message lines `generated by llmgit` and `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`; the latter is explicit AI co-authorship on the BIC itself.
evidence: Advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v2jj-5g64-rxp4 names Management API shellExecCommand command injection, says affected through 1.4.1, and lists patched versions as unknown; first-party report https://github.com/chenhg5/cc-connect/issues/1489 gives the POST /api/v1/cron exec chain, and maintainer chenhg5 explicitly confirms the empty-token authentication branch, cron exec acceptance, shell sink, all-interface port 9820 binding, and working create/force-exec PoC. In the validated clone, `git show --format=fuller --stat --patch c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380` shows one parent 968cd9142dd7a9f7f1ea09a45cb7329761c44abb and adds core/management.go, cmd/cc-connect/main.go wiring, and ManagementConfig: Start uses Addr fmt.Sprintf(":%d", m.port); wrap calls authenticate; authenticate returns true when m.token == ""; POST handleCron accepts CronAddRequest and assigns Exec: req.Exec. `git log -L 325,339:core/management.go HEAD` traces that authentication function unchanged to c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380; all-ref `git log -S 'if m.token == ""' -- core/management.go` and `git log -S 'req.Exec' -- core/management.go` independently identify the same first writer. Direct parent verification: `git ls-tree 968cd9142dd7a9f7f1ea09a45cb7329761c44abb -- core/management.go` returns no entry, while `git grep -n 'job.Exec' 968cd9142dd7a9f7f1ea09a45cb7329761c44abb -- core/engine.go` shows the pre-existing sink at line 613 as exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", job.Exec); thus the parent lacks the exposed route/auth flaw although the downstream shell capability exists. Version boundary: `git tag --contains c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 --sort=version:refname` begins at v1.2.2-beta.2; `git ls-tree v1.2.2-beta.1^{} -- core/management.go` is empty, while `git grep` finds the empty-token branch and Exec assignment in v1.2.2-beta.2, v1.4.1, v1.5.0, and v1.5.1-beta.1. The advisory's upper bound is therefore stale/incomplete: repository tags after 1.4.1 remain vulnerable. At audit time HEAD 80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4 (the v1.5.1-beta.1 target) still has core/management.go:326-327 returning true for an empty token and line 1574 assigning req.Exec, with core/engine.go:2067 passing job.Exec to shellExecCommand and line 7970 invoking the configured shell with the command flag. No fix is present: the all-ref empty-token pickaxe has no removal commit, the vulnerable code persists at the newest tag/HEAD, GHSA has no patched version/source fix, and issue #1489 was closed only by the stale bot without remediation. Finally, `git cat-file -p c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380` reproduces the BIC-only AI marker exactly: `generated by llmgit` and `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
reasoning: The vulnerability requires three facts: an unauthenticated network entry, attacker control of a cron job's Exec value, and shell interpretation of that value. Earlier commits supplied intentional local cron shell execution, but the direct parent of c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 had no Management API file or route. Commit c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 atomically supplied the missing remote boundary and made blank token mean allow all while forwarding the request's Exec field to the existing shell scheduler, so it is the first complete and smallest advisory-specific BIC. Later manual-trigger work only shortened time-to-execution and did not originate the flaw. Parent-tree absence, -L history, two independent -S pickaxes, and tag snapshots agree. The flaw remains unpatched through v1.5.1-beta.1/HEAD, justifying null fix fields rather than inventing the dispatched-but-never-landed v1.4.2 fix. Because the BIC commit object itself explicitly credits Claude as co-author and the BIC first writes the causally flawed Management API mechanism, the closed verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE rather than AI_CODE_FLAWED or NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: unpatched; no upstream fix commit or patched release exists in the validated all-ref history through HEAD 80713167d17b3f2a3906efc3b14b3acab39766e4 / v1.5.1-beta.1, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are necessarily null
